dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Chase-A-Bag is at risk due to behavior concerns. He was returned to the care centers due to a multiple bite history. His previous owner reported that he has bitten three times in the last three months. All three bites were bite-and-releases that left punctures wounds and were treated at home. He was also described as an active and playful dog. While in care he has allowed some handling and takes treats readily with a soft body. Medically, he has dental disease.

Chase-a-Bag was first surrendered to the care center in July 2026 as his owner was not able to care for him, and was returned to the care center in October 2026 for behavioral issues. Chase-a-Bag is described as an active, playful dog who knows several cues and likes to go on 1-2 walks a day. He has shown social behavior with staff while at the care center. Chase-a-Bag is reported to have bitten three times in his previous home, twice while being pet and once when the owner was attempting to remove him from a crate. These were bite and release incidents that left small punctures and were treated at home. Chase-a-Bag is also reported to growl and snap when the owners take food from him, and to bark and lunge at children and other dogs on walks. Due to the concerns reported in the previous home, the behavior department recommends that Chase-a-Bag be placed with a New Hope placement partner who can provide an experienced adult-only foster home that can provide him with a period of decompression, necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based), and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
